title: The Cowpens, January 1781: a WarMapper reconstruction
label: 1781 (reconstructed)
about: This is a WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map: no map of 1781 shows this ground. The roads are those Edwin Bearss drew in 1967 as the roads of the battle, laid on the ground by the road the park still keeps, and beyond his sheet the roads of the 1959 survey on the lines Mills's map of 1825 gives. The ground is today's, which the park has kept much as it was; the streams are today's. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.
notes: Inside Bearss's sheet the roads are good to about 25-50 m: his road matches the park's trace to 4 m at the median, and his other roads lie within 20-50 m of the roads of 1959. Beyond it they are roads of 1959 (and, for Tarleton's approach, today's Green River Road), rated low. Bearss shows no other roads, houses or fields; the ground was open woods, pastured, with no undergrowth (S107, p. 8).
credit: WarMapper reconstruction from Bearss, 1967 (National Park Service), the USGS sheets of 1959 and 1975, and Mills, 1825

title: South Carolina, 1775 to 1781: a WarMapper reconstruction
label: 1775 (reconstructed)
about: This is a WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map. Its lines are those of Henry Mouzon's map of the two Carolinas (1775), laid on today's ground: the rivers and the sea coast fitted to today's courses, which they keep, and the main roads and boundary lines carried with them. Mouzon's map was made for the colonies' trade and land grants, not as a survey: his roads are good to a few kilometres, his up-country less. A first pilot: only the main lines are traced. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.
notes: Rivers and coast good to about 1-2 km where today's river is in Natural Earth; roads and boundaries to 3-5 km; the far north-west (the Cherokee country) to no better than 10 km. Not yet traced: inlets, islands and sounds, swamps, the lesser roads, ferries and fords, and the towns, which the orientation's places mark.
credit: WarMapper reconstruction from Mouzon, 1775 (Library of Congress), fitted with Natural Earth
